note: Track hearing-changes (theory-ear), step 4: the 1, 4, 5 and 6 mixed, in a new order, then with chords held for two bars, then in three new keys. Missing: backing-track cannot hide its chord boxes (the text asks the player to look away) and plays a fixed order, not a new one each round.

exercise.title: 1, 4, 5 and 6 in any order
exercise.why: Each chord of a key keeps its own distance from home, so the 4, the 5 and the 6 sound the same in any order and in any key once you hear them against the 1.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track: the 1, 4, 5 and 6 of one key, in a new order. Look away from the chord boxes and call out the number on each change, then look at the lit box to check.
If you lose your place, wait for the 1 and start again from there.

Press Play below to start the backing track: a longer round, and some chords stay for two bars, so you can't count your way to the next change. Look away and call out the number only when you hear the chord move, then look to check.
Practice until you can name a chord before its bar is over.

Press Play below to start the backing track, in a new key. Listen to the first chord, the 1, then look away and call out the numbers.
Once the number comes as each chord starts, try another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Play to start the backing track again.
When you change the key, the chords are new but each number sits at the same distance from home.
